categories.name: Photo walks
categories.description: Walks around the hill with a camera.

posts.title: Loading film without fear
posts.excerpt: Out of the light, tongue to the spool, two blank frames. Loading a film camera takes a minute once you have done it with someone watching.
posts.content:
Turn your back to the sun, open the camera and drop the canister in. Pull the tongue across to the take-up spool and push it into a slot, then wind once and check that the teeth hold both edges of the film.

Close the back, wind and fire twice. If the rewind knob turns as you wind, the film is moving. That is all; bring the camera by the counter and we will do it with you the first time.

posts.title: The persimmon walk
posts.excerpt: Every October we take a test roll down the hill while the persimmons turn orange. Thirty-six frames, one hour, one street.
posts.content:
The light on the hill is low and warm in autumn, which is kind to old lenses. We meter for the shadows, keep the speed at one sixty and let the fruit glow.

Join the next walk from the shop door; bring any film camera, or borrow one from the shelf for the afternoon.

posts.title: What happens to your roll
posts.excerpt: From the counter to the tank to the scanner: three days in the lab, and why we hang every film to dry overnight.
posts.content:
Your roll gets an envelope with your name and a number. In the dark we wind it onto a reel, then it spends its time in the tank: developer, stop, fixer, a long rinse.

It hangs overnight so it dries flat and clean. In the morning we cut it into strips of six, scan every frame and print the ones you asked for.
